Subject: Question: how do you bill when we chain two models + minimums?

Hi Tessa,

Quick one from finance as we prepare the SOW: our product pipeline has an encoder model that creates a 6k token context and then we invoke a smaller assistant model with that context + a short user prompt. Two questions:

2) What rounding/minimum rules apply for short assistant calls? Our assistant calls are often 30–80 tokens — how does the minimum quantum or rounding affect unit spend?

Subject: Re: Question: how do you bill when we chain two models + minimums?

Hi Liam / Sarah — thanks for the sample, that helped. Short answer up front: by default tokens are metered at the model invocation level (so a token sent to Model A and then again to Model B in a separate invocation will be billed twice), but there are two levers that change practical cost: session-level KV/prefix reuse and committed-tenant rounding quanta.

Illustrative examples (numbers simplified):
- Pipeline: Encoder produces 6,000 tokens; Assistant call sends those 6,000 tokens + 40 new user tokens.
  - If you call the assistant as a separate model invocation, standard hosted billing meters 6,000 tokens for the encoder call + 6,040 tokens for the assistant call = 12,040 billable tokens.
  - If you enable session-level KV/prefix reuse (available on Dedicated / Private or via the "prefix dedupe" option on certain hosted SKUs), the platform caches the encoder output and the assistant call can reference the cached KV instead of re-sending the full 6k. In that case we bill the encoder 6,000 tokens and the assistant only for the 40 new prompt/response tokens => 6,040 total.

Rounding and minimums:
- Hosted (self-serve) tier: we meter per-call and then apply a per-invocation quantum of 100 tokens for short calls — i.e., any call <=100 tokens is rounded up to 100 tokens. That avoids microbilling noise for unpredictable traffic.
- Dedicated/Committed customers: quantum is negotiable; typical committed customers get a 10-token quantum for short calls, and we can go to 1-token microbilling for large enterprise true-ups.

So for your 40-token assistant call:
- Hosted default: billed as 100 tokens (unless prefix dedupe in play).
- Dedicated with 10-token quantum: billed as 40 tokens rounded up to 40 (already multiple of 10) — effectively 40.

Prefix reuse caveat: prefix dedupe works when both invocations are part of the same session and the model variants are compatible with our cache keying (same tokenizer family and compatible quantization). If you do an out-of-band second call (different session or different cluster region), we cannot guarantee dedupe.

Discount/retro credit: we do not automatically apply retroactive credits for usage already invoiced, but for pilots converting to committed business we frequently grant a pilot consumption rebate or one-time credit as part of the amendment. If you share the invoice range and target commit, we can model a rebate.

I'll put Vanessa (account lead) and Markus (billing) on the thread to propose a simple amendment and a sample invoice mapping.

Best,
Tessa Morgan

1) A) 20% committed discount from sign date: APPROVE subject to a 12-month minimum ARR commit. We should model net ARR with renewals; if approved we will include the discount in the SOW.

2) B) One-time pilot rebate: APPROVE up to 50% of the estimated delta for June (quantified on the attached proposed_amendment_draft.pdf). We should cap the rebate ($20k cap) to avoid open-ended exposure.

3) C) Short-call quantum reduction (100 -> 10 tokens) for first 3 months: APPROVE for Dedicated/Committed SKUs only (we cannot change hosted global quantum by tenant without infra changes). This will be in the amendment as a temporary override.

If this is okay, I will: (a) send Liam a short email confirming A/B/C with the cap and commit condition; (b) attach a 1‑page amendment and a sample invoice mapping; (c) create a HubSpot task (see link) and open a billing true-up ticket for Markus to estimate the rebate.
